question: Which type of mountains In the northwest, north and northeast bind India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Young fold mountains.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **India is bounded by the Himalayas in the northwest, north and northeast.**
 
• The **Himalayas **are known as **young fold mountains** because they started to form in the Late Cretaceous to Tertiary era and are still rising in elevation.
 
• Due to the compressive forces created when the Asian and Indian/Australian continental plates collided, these mountains are known as fold mountains.
 
• Sedimentary rocks make up the Himalayan region.
 
• The average height of mountain peaks in the Himalayan region is about 6000 meters.
 
• It is the longest and most northern range and it is made up of snow glaciers and is coated in snow.
 
• It is made of granite and is symmetrical by nature and it has imposing mountains like Nanda Devi and Kanchenjunga.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Block mountains: **

 
 
• Block Mountains formed as the result of faulting caused by tensile and compressive forces motored by endogenetic forces coming from within the earth, also known as fault-block mountains.
 
• Block mountains repre­sent the upstanding parts of the ground between two faults or on either side of a rift valley or a graben.
 
 
 
• **Dome mountains:**
 
 
• Dome mountains are formed where a region of flat-lying sedimentary rocks is warped or bowed upward making a structural dome.
 
• Their topography is characterized by a relatively flat, dissected surface sloping gradually toward the surrounding lowlands, or basins.
 
• The diameters of the bases of dome mountains range up to hundreds of kilometres.
 
 
 
• **Plateau mountains:**
 
 
• Plateau mountains occur in series when the folds of a mountain chain pass abruptly into the horizontal strata of a basalt plateau that is largely denuded of trees and eroded.
